    To tackle the aforementioned challenges, we present               thermore, ShowUI [38] introduces a Visual Token Selection
MP-GUI, a dual visual-clues MLLM for visual GUI un-                   approach to reduce computational costs. It also integrates
derstanding. MP-GUI extracts graphical, textual, and spa-             various GUI tasks in a systematic manner, aiming to effec-
tial modality signals from the screen using three perceivers.         tively guide the MLLM [55] in learning domain knowledge.
This design reinforces the model’s capability to grasp both           Generally, for most research on solving domain-specific
visual and textual modalities by integrating spatial informa-         multi-modal tasks, the dense image features generated by
tion, improving overall screen perception. Notably, each              the vision backbone are the sole vision clues provided to
type of GUI understanding task may have distinct screen               the LLM. Given the distinctiveness of GUI scenarios, we
content preferences [7, 23, 35]. Thus, MP-GUI includes                introduce a dual-visual-clues framework, which provides
a Fusion Gate that adaptively combines screen signals of              the LLM with additional GUI-tailored visual clues, thus en-
different modalities, enabling task-oriented feature fusion.          hancing the screen perception capabilities of the MLLM.
Unlike current end-to-end implicit training[15, 38], we de-
sign a training recipe including a Multi-stage Training Strat-
egy and matching training objectives, especially a novel              2.2. GUI Understanding
Spatial Relationship Prediction task and a data synthesis
                                                                      GUI understanding involves a full range of downstream
pipeline, which explicitly guides the model to learn GUI
                                                                      tasks, such as screen grounding [6, 15], widget cap-
knowledge. Extensive experiments on various GUI-related
                                                                      tioning [35], screen question answering [5, 12], naviga-
benchmarks showcase the robust performance of MP-GUI.
                                                                      tion [18, 50], screen summarization [54], etc. Consid-

                                                                      ering the huge difference between GUI and general vi-

GUI perception and understanding capability.

                                                                       Task Semantic Signal

Figure 2. Overview of our MP-GUI. MP-GUI consists of three parts: (1) a vision backbone providing visual clues of the screenshot; (2) a
TGS-Perception Fusion Module including three GUI-tailored perceivers for extracting specific GUI modality signals and a Fusion Gate for
dynamically fusing these signals based on task semantics to produce GUI-tailored visual clues; and (3) an LLM generating results relying
on screen visual clues, GUI-tailored visual clues, and task semantic signal.

to guide the TxP to focus on textual signals within screens.                      dataset for small objects derived from AITW [50]. Specifi-

                                                                          In this paper, we center on enhancing MLLM in GUI sce-
5.4. Qualitative Analysis                                                 narios and present MP-GUI, a dual-visual-clues model. It
In Fig. 5, we display several examples on basic GUI under-                uses three GUI-specific perceivers to extract modality sig-
standing tasks (Sec. 5.1). The results demonstrate that our               nals from the screen and a FG module to fuse them based on
MP-GUI effectively understands the implicit knowledge on                  task semantics, generating additional GUI-tailored visual
the screen, including graphics, text, and their spatial rela-             clues to enhance MLLM’s GUI visual perception. We also
tionships (case a). For queries that necessitate deeper rea-              introduce a novel SRP task for explicitly modeling GUI ele-
soning (case b), MP-GUI can effectively locates and as-                   ments’ spatial relationships and an automated synthetic data
sociates details from different areas to generate accurate                pipeline for FG training. Extensive experiments confirm our
answers. Furthermore, MP-GUI demonstrates a compre-                       designs significantly enhance MLLM’s GUI understanding,
hensive ability to capture essential modality details of the              facilitating the improvement of various downstream tasks.
screen (case c). Notably, MP-GUI’s advanced GUI per-                         Acknowledgments This work was supported by the Na-
ception and understanding capabilities can alleviate the hal-             tional Natural Science Foundation of China (Grant No.6237
lucination problem often encountered in MLLMs (case d).                   2408). This work was also supported by Ant Group.

                                                                                        F.2. MPE-QA
                                                                                              The prompt for Global Description

                                                                                              Generate a summary of the screen
                                                                                              in one sentence. Do not focus on
                                                                                              specifically naming the various
                                                                                              UI elements, but instead, focus on
                                                                                              the content.

prehension capabilities. The Graphical Perceiver boosts
the model’s capacity to center on smaller areas. In con-
trast, Llama3.2-V(11B) [3], Qwen2-VL(7B) [55], and In-
ternVL2(8B) [14] are influenced by the sizable ’12:30’ in
the middle of the screen (as seen in Example 4). It is note-
worthy that even when the question is unanswerable, as
shown in the second example, our method still functions
robustly.
Complex ScreenQA. The Spatial Perceiver enhances the
awareness of spatial relationships between GUI elements on
the screen. Compared with other MLLMs, our MP-GUI has
advantages in difference calculation (as shown in Examples
1 and 4) and quantity counting (as shown in Examples 2 and
3) in Fig. 13. More qualitative results of our MP-GUI are
shown in Fig. 14.
